name: Janelle S Bynum

positions.statement: On her campaign housing page, Bynum says she has worked with both parties on efforts to lower the cost of housing.
positions.excerpt: Janelle has worked with both parties on efforts to lower the cost of housing

positions.statement: In a May 2026 release, Bynum said three of her bills in the House-passed H.R. 6644 housing package would help build housing and lower costs.
positions.excerpt: These bills put us on track to build the housing we need to finally lower costs.

source.publisher: Office of U.S. Rep. Janelle Bynum

positions.statement: On her campaign homelessness page, Bynum says that in Congress she is continuing work to end homelessness.
positions.excerpt: In Congress, she is continuing the work to end homelessness in our communities.

positions.statement: Her office's May 2026 release says the House-passed housing package included her Incentivizing Local Solutions to Homelessness Act.
positions.excerpt: Incentivizing Local Solutions to Homelessness Act

source.publisher: Office of U.S. Rep. Janelle Bynum

positions.statement: On her campaign climate page, Bynum is described as supporting more clean energy and a transition away from fossil fuels.
positions.excerpt: She is supporting efforts to generate more clean energy

positions.statement: Her official issues page lists a July 2026 release saying Bynum introduced legislation to improve electricity price transparency.

positions.statement: In a May 2026 release, Bynum says she has been working in Congress to prepare for and respond to wildfires.

source.publisher: Office of U.S. Rep. Janelle Bynum

positions.statement: On her campaign page, Bynum is described as fighting in Congress to defend reproductive rights and codify Roe v. Wade.
positions.excerpt: In Congress, she is fighting to defend reproductive rights and codify Roe v. Wade at the federal level.

positions.statement: Her official issues page says her top priorities are lowering costs, creating more jobs, and improving Oregonians' quality of life.

positions.statement: A February 2026 release from Bynum's office says she celebrated $1,092,000 in funding for an Oregon City water transmission main project.
positions.excerpt: The Congresswoman first celebrated $1,092,000 in funding for the Water Transmission Main Project at Oregon City Hall

positions.excerpt: I’ll never vote to hurt our farmers or our rural communities.

source.publisher: Office of U.S. Rep. Janelle Bynum

positions.statement: KTVZ reported in June 2025 that three of Bynum's bipartisan small-business bills passed the House and moved to the Senate.
positions.excerpt: Three of her bipartisan bills aimed at helping small businesses pass the House and are now headed to the U.S. Senate.

positions.statement: A March 2026 release says Bynum introduced the Supporting VA Families Act, which would guarantee unpaid parental leave for all VA employees.

positions.statement: An April 2025 release from Bynum's office quotes her saying families cannot afford to pay more for groceries, gas or other everyday items because of tariffs.

positions.excerpt: introduced a bill on Friday aiming to help small businesses impacted by tariffs imposed by the Trump administration.

collection_notes: Identity: all items are about the incumbent U.S. Representative for OR-05 (bynum.house.gov and janellebynum.com, the site verified via the voters' pamphlet). The agriculture item (Farm Bill vote) is from her office's press release with no roll call number shown, so it is in positions, not voting_record; the electricity price transparency item rests on a headline on her official issues page. The wildfire/housing excerpts are copied from fetched pages; some source quotes use curly apostrophes.
